Godly Jealousy
JEL-uh-see
noun phrase
From the Greek theou zelos, “jealousy of God,” the holy zeal that guards the purity of God’s people for Christ their husband.

📖 Biblical Definition

Godly jealousy is the holy zeal, modelled upon the jealousy of God Himself, by which a faithful pastor guards the purity of Christ’s people for Christ their husband. The apostle Paul writes to the Corinthians, For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ (2Co 11:2). The dictionary marks the distinction between this and the sinful jealousy of envy. Carnal jealousy is a work of the flesh (Gal 5:20), a grudging of another’s good; but godly jealousy is a fruit of love, a zeal for the honour of the beloved. So the LORD reveals Himself as a jealous God (Exo 20:5), not with the petty envy of men, but with the holy zeal of a husband who will not share His glory with another. Paul, set as the friend of the bridegroom, fears lest, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so their minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ (2Co 11:3). The dictionary commends godly jealousy as the proper affection of every faithful soul: a holy fear of any rival to Christ that would draw the bride from her one husband. So the Scripture teaches that love for Christ is rightly jealous; that to be at ease while error courts the church is no virtue but a failure of love; and that the truest tenderness toward God’s people is the zeal that keeps them chaste unto Christ alone.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The holy zeal, modelled on God’s own jealousy, that guards the purity of Christ’s people for Christ their husband.

expand to see more

GODLY JEALOUSY, the holy zeal that guards God’s people for Christ.

It is modelled on the jealousy of God, who will not share His glory with another.

It differs from carnal jealousy, which is a work of the flesh.

Paul was jealous over the church to present her a chaste virgin to Christ.

It is the proper affection of every faithful shepherd and soul.

📖 Key Scripture

2Co 11:2 — "For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ."

2Co 11:3 — "But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ."

Exo 20:5 — "Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;"

Exo 34:14 — "For thou shalt worship no other god: for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God:"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A holy affection little redefined; it recovers jealousy as the zeal of love that keeps the church chaste unto Christ.

expand to see more

Godly jealousy has drawn little redefinition from the present age, though jealousy as a word is now reckoned wholly a vice, so that the holy sense is forgotten. The dictionary records it that the reader may distinguish the carnal jealousy of envy from the godly jealousy of love, which guards the beloved’s honour.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that love for Christ is rightly jealous. The LORD calls Himself a jealous God, not with the petty envy of men but with the holy zeal of a husband who will not share His bride with idols; and the faithful pastor, as the friend of the bridegroom, is jealous over the church to keep her chaste unto Christ alone. So the saint is taught that to be at ease while error courts the church is no virtue but a failure of love, and that the truest tenderness toward God’s people is the zeal that guards them from every rival to their one husband.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Greek for “jealousy of God,” the phrase names the holy zeal that guards the church for Christ.

Godly Jealousy — Greek theou zelos, “jealousy of God.”

It is the holy zeal modelled on God’s own jealousy.

It differs from carnal jealousy, which is a work of the flesh.

It guards the church to present her a chaste virgin to Christ.

It is the proper affection of every faithful shepherd and soul.

Usage

"I am jealous over you with godly jealousy, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ."

"The LORD, whose name is Jealous, will not share His glory with another."

"Godly jealousy is the zeal of love that keeps the church chaste unto Christ alone."
